Lagrange four-square theorem

Words: 16
Number theory OurBigBook.com
The Lagrange four-square theorem says that every nonnegative integer is a sum of four integer squares.

Arithmetic function

Words: 591 Articles: 27
Number theory OurBigBook.com
An arithmetic function is a function whose domain is the positive integers, usually taking values in the complex numbers.

Multiplicative arithmetic function

Words: 187 Articles: 8
Arithmetic function OurBigBook.com
An arithmetic function f is multiplicative when f(mn)=f(m)f(n) whenever m and n are coprime.

Completely multiplicative function

Words: 21
Multiplicative arithmetic function OurBigBook.com
An arithmetic function f is completely multiplicative when f(mn)=f(m)f(n) for every pair of positive integers m,n, without a coprimality condition.

Divisor sum

Words: 38 Articles: 1
Multiplicative arithmetic function OurBigBook.com
The divisor sum of an arithmetic function f is
F(n)=∑d∣n​f(d).
(1)
If f is multiplicative, then F is multiplicative as well.

Words: 17
Divisor sum OurBigBook.com
The sum-of-divisors function is
σ1​(n)=∑d∣n​d.
(2)
It is the divisor sum of the identity arithmetic function n↦n.

Pretentious distance (D(f,g;x))

Words: 114 Articles: 4
Multiplicative arithmetic function OurBigBook.com
For multiplicative functions bounded by one, the pretentious distance up to x is defined by
D(f,g;x)2=∑p≤x​p1−ℜ(f(p)g(p)​)​.
(3)
It measures how similarly f and g behave on primes.
Triangle inequality for pretentious distance
Words: 9
Pretentious distance OurBigBook.com
The pretentious distance obeys
D(f1​f2​,g1​g2​;x)≤D(f1​,g1​;x)+D(f2​,g2​;x).
(4)
Archimedean character (nit)
Words: 20
Pretentious distance OurBigBook.com
An Archimedean character on the positive integers is the completely multiplicative function n↦nit for a real parameter t.
Halász theorem
Words: 27
Pretentious distance OurBigBook.com
Halász's theorem bounds the mean of a bounded multiplicative arithmetic function in terms of its least pretentious distance from an Archimedean character. A large mean can occur only when this distance is small.
Strong aperiodicity of the Möbius function
Words: 29
Pretentious distance OurBigBook.com
The Möbius function stays far in pretentious distance from every Archimedean character. One useful uniform form is
inf∣t∣≤2(logx)1/10​D(μ,nit;x)2⟶∞.
(5)
This follows by estimating the prime sum ∑p≤x​(1+cos(tlogp))/p.

Dirichlet convolution (∗)

Words: 118 Articles: 4
Arithmetic function OurBigBook.com
The Dirichlet convolution of arithmetic functions f and g is
(f∗g)(n)=∑d∣n​f(d)g(n/d).
(6)
It is associative and commutative, its identity is the function supported at 1, and the Möbius function is the convolution inverse of the constant-one function.

Constant-one arithmetic function (1)

Words: 20
Dirichlet convolution OurBigBook.com
The constant-one arithmetic function has 1(n)=1 for every positive integer n. Its Dirichlet convolution with f is the divisor sum (1∗f)(n)=∑d∣n​f(d).

Identity arithmetic function (id)

Words: 17
Dirichlet convolution OurBigBook.com
The identity arithmetic function is id(n)=n. The identity id=1∗φ is equivalent to ∑d∣n​φ(d)=n.

Identity for Dirichlet convolution (ε)

Words: 17
Dirichlet convolution OurBigBook.com
The identity for Dirichlet convolution is ε(1)=1 and ε(n)=0 for n>1. It satisfies f∗ε=f for every arithmetic function f.

Dirichlet convolution OurBigBook.com
The Dirichlet hyperbola method evaluates a summatory Dirichlet convolution by splitting the lattice points ab≤x at a,b≤x​. For the divisor function,
∑n≤x​τ(n)=2∑a≤x​​⌊ax​⌋−⌊x​⌋2.

Von Mangoldt function (Λ(n))

Words: 169 Articles: 6
Arithmetic function OurBigBook.com
The Von Mangoldt function is Λ(n)=logp when n is a positive power of a prime number p, and is zero otherwise.

Von Mangoldt divisor identity

Words: 18
Von Mangoldt function OurBigBook.com
For every positive integer n,
∑d∣n​Λ(d)=logn.
(8)
Equivalently, the constant-one function convolved with the Von Mangoldt function is the natural logarithm.

Analytic number theory

Words: 2k Articles: 68
Number theory OurBigBook.com
Analytic number theory studies integers, prime numbers, and arithmetic functions using tools from real analysis and complex analysis, especially Dirichlet series and their singularities.

Landau theorem for a Dirichlet series with nonnegative coefficients

Words: 45
Analytic number theory OurBigBook.com
If a Dirichlet series with nonnegative coefficients has finite abscissa of convergence σc​, then the function it defines has a singularity at the real point s=σc​. Consequently, if that function extends holomorphically across every real point, the original series converges for every real s.

Nonvanishing of a nonprincipal Dirichlet L-function at one

Words: 35
Analytic number theory OurBigBook.com
For every nonprincipal Dirichlet character χ,
L(1,χ)=0.
(17)
Multiply the Dirichlet L-functions over every character modulo q. The resulting Euler product has nonnegative coefficients. A zero at one would cancel the principal factor's pole and contradict the Landau theorem for a Dirichlet series with nonnegative coefficients.

ψ(x;q,a)=∑n≤xn≡a(modq)​​Λ(n).
(18)
The Orthogonality of Dirichlet characters expresses it in terms of character-twisted Von Mangoldt functions.

Classical zero-free region for Dirichlet L-functions

Words: 127 Articles: 3
Analytic number theory OurBigBook.com
There is an absolute c>0 such that the Dirichlet L-functions modulo q have no zero in
ℜs≥1−log(q(∣ℑs∣+2))c​
(19)
apart from at most one real simple zero belonging to a real nonprincipal character.

An exceptional zero is the possible real simple zero β omitted from the otherwise uniform Classical zero-free region for Dirichlet L-functions. It belongs to a real nonprincipal primitive Dirichlet character and satisfies β<1.

Let N=pq for distinct odd prime numbers p,q with gcd(p−1,q−1)=10. Exactly 100 unit bases make N a Fermat pseudoprime, and exactly 50 of these make it a strong pseudoprime. The Fermat bases form C10​×C10​ under the Chinese remainder theorem for unit groups. If N−1=2sm, then 5∣m and m is odd, so the mth-power map sends five elements of each C10​ to 1 and five to −1. The strong condition requires equal signs in both components, giving 52+52=50.

Euler witnesses occupy at least half the unit bases

Words: 57
Euler witness OurBigBook.com
If one Euler witness b0​ exists modulo N, multiplication by b0​ injects the set of nonwitnesses into the set of witnesses. Indeed, the product of b0​ with a nonwitness cannot be another nonwitness, because cancellation and multiplicativity of the Jacobi symbol would make b0​ a nonwitness. Thus at least half of the units modulo N are Euler witnesses.

Existence of an Euler witness for every odd composite integer

Words: 63
Euler witness OurBigBook.com
Every odd composite integer has an Euler witness. For a nonsquarefree integer, a base congruent to 1+p modulo a repeated prime factor p2 fails the Euler congruence by the binomial theorem. For a squarefree integer, use the Chinese remainder theorem to choose a base that is a quadratic nonresidue modulo one prime factor and 1 modulo another. Its Jacobi symbol is −1, while its power is 1 modulo the second factor.

Reduction algorithm for a positive definite binary quadratic form

Words: 75

For a positive definite integral form [a,b,c], a unimodular shear can replace b by its representative b′ with ∣b′∣≤a. If the resulting c′=(b′2−D)/(4a) is smaller than a, swapping the variables replaces the leading coefficient by the smaller positive integer c′. Repeating terminates and produces ∣b∣≤a≤c; determinant-one sign changes enforce the boundary convention. Thus every positive definite integral binary quadratic form is properly equivalent to a reduced form.
